one_liner: 2015 benchmark of normal-sample generators; Ziggurat and AVX Box-Muller run 2.8-8x faster than std::normal_distribution with minstd_rand.
what_it_does: A benchmark harness, not a library: each algorithm is a small source file exposing normaldistf(float*, size_t n) / normaldist(double*, size_t n) that fills a buffer with standard-normal samples, registered with a REGISTER_TEST macro. It times Box-Muller, Marsaglia polar, Ziggurat (Jochen Voss's GSL-style code), Acklam inverse CDF, central-limit sums, SSE2/AVX Box-Muller and CLT, and std::normal_distribution, and checks mean, SD, skewness and excess kurtosis of 1M samples. To reuse one, you copy the function plus src/lcg.h (and sse_mathfun.h / avx_mathfun.h for the SIMD variants).
how_it_is_fast: Ziggurat (Marsaglia-Tsang 2000) covers the density with 128 equal-area layers, so about 99% of samples cost one 32-bit draw, a table lookup, a multiply and a compare; log/exp are needed only in the rare wedge and tail cases. The SSE2/AVX Box-Muller variants run 4 or 8 lanes of a 32-bit LCG and use vectorized log and sincos approximations from sse_mathfun/avx_mathfun, producing 8 or 16 floats per loop iteration. Every non-std variant uses a one-multiply LCG (Numerical Recipes constants for 32-bit, a 64-bit LCG for double) as the uniform source, which is far cheaper than minstd_rand plus uniform_real_distribution.
when_to_use: Choosing a normal-sampling algorithm: the table shows how Box-Muller, polar, inverse CDF, CLT and Ziggurat compare under the same cheap uniform source
Bulk float fills (Monte Carlo noise, procedural generation) on x86 with AVX where approximate log/sincos accuracy is acceptable: boxmuller_avx reached 2.25 ns/sample
A scalar Ziggurat for float or double when you can accept GPL-2.0-or-later code or will rewrite it
As a starting harness to benchmark your own normal sampler against std::normal_distribution
when_not_to_use: Statistically sensitive work: the uniform source is a power-of-two LCG, and the Ziggurat takes its layer index and sign from the LCG's lowest 8 bits, which cycle with period 128/256
Projects that cannot take copyleft code: src/ziggurat.cpp is GPL-2.0-or-later even though the repo is MIT
Code that needs a reusable sampler object: each call re-creates the generator at a fixed seed, so every call returns the same sequence and there is no seeding API
The CLT variants: they fail the repo's own kurtosis check, and clt*_avx has a buffer-overrun bug (see gotchas)
Non-x86 targets or modern CPUs without retesting: SIMD paths are SSE2/AVX intrinsics only, and the only published numbers are from a 2012 Core i5 with clang 6.1

integration.dependencies: none for scalar variants; sse_mathfun.h / avx_mathfun.h (zlib license, vendored in src/) for SSE2/AVX variants; premake4 to build the harness
integration.platforms: x86/x86-64; the AVX variants need AVX (the 8-lane LCG emulates 256-bit integer multiply with SSE4.1 _mm_mullo_epi32); scalar code is portable
integration.thread_safety: Each call uses its own stack-local LCG, so concurrent calls are safe but all return the identical sequence; not documented by the author

gotchas: Alignment and size: boxmuller_sse2 needs 16-byte-aligned data and n % 8 == 0; boxmuller_avx needs 32-byte alignment and n % 16 == 0 (the code asserts 16, not 8); scalar boxmuller and polar need even n

clt_avx steps the index by 4 while storing 8 floats per iteration, so it does twice the work and the last store writes 16 bytes past the end of the buffer; the harness's 32-byte slack may not cover it

Not like-for-like with std: libc++'s normal_distribution is itself the Marsaglia polar method, and the repo's own polar method with the cheap LCG is already 2.5x faster than cpp11random in double, so most of the headline gap is the uniform source, not the algorithm (derived from page data)
The SIMD lanes are seeded 1..4 or 1..8 with the same LCG constants, so lanes are linearly related; output is not suitable where independence between samples matters
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Use it to compare algorithms or to borrow a minimal Ziggurat or SIMD Box-Muller kernel; for production sampling, Zest (generalized Ziggurat, reported 3.6x over STL normal) or EigenRand (vectorized std-like distributions) give a maintained API with a proper engine. An open issue (#3, 2020) posts a faster single-table Ziggurat (about 4.0 ns vs 7.3-7.8 ns for the repo's version).
verified_claims_summary: On an iMac Core i5-3330S (2.7 GHz) with clang 6.1 and libc++, best of 10 runs of 1M samples: double cpp11random (std::normal_distribution + std::minstd_rand) 32.2 ns/sample vs Ziggurat 7.1 ns (4.55x); float 18.6 ns vs Ziggurat 6.7 ns (about 2.8x) and boxmuller_avx 2.25 ns (about 8.3x, derived from page data). Against the same-LCG polar method, Ziggurat's own algorithmic gain is about 1.6-1.8x (derived from page data).
status_note: Abandoned since July 2015 (one open PR and two open issues from 2019-2020); the MIT harness and SIMD kernels are small enough to copy, but the Ziggurat file is GPL-2.0-or-later and needs a better uniform generator before reuse.
